title: Saudi Arabia | SAMA Compliance Function, Governance and Whistleblowing
tagline: Run compliance, board governance, senior appointments and speak-up channels the way SAMA expects at a conventional Saudi bank.
sectors: Conventional commercial banks in Saudi Arabia
Foreign bank branches in Saudi Arabia
Bank boards, board committees and company secretaries
Compliance, internal audit and risk functions
description:
This quest teaches the compliance and governance rules the **Saudi Central Bank (SAMA)** sets for conventional banks. It is based on SAMA's **Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks Operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia** (2020), the **Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions** (version 2, 2024), the **Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions**, the **Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions** (2019) and SAMA's professional certification circulars, all published in the SAMA Rulebook.

Paragraph 72 of the compliance principles requires an annual compliance training and awareness programme for all employees, compliance training for new joiners before they start, and periodic reminders for staff who deal with the public. The governance principles require an induction for every board member, and the whistleblowing policy requires awareness programmes on reporting channels and protection. This quest supports those duties for all bank staff, and in depth for compliance, audit, governance and senior staff.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own policies, procedures or the latest SAMA instructions; always follow them. It covers conventional banking only.
audience: All employees of conventional banks in Saudi Arabia, including new joiners before they start their duties
Compliance officers, compliance unit staff and staff of violation reports units
Board members, board committee members, board secretaries and governance staff
Senior executives and candidates for posts that need SAMA's non-objection
Internal auditors and risk managers who review compliance and governance
outcomes: Explain how SAMA's compliance principles divide duties between the board, senior management, the compliance unit and every employee
Apply the independence, reporting, non-objection, pay and delegation rules for the Chief Compliance Officer and compliance unit
Describe board composition, independence, induction and committee rules in SAMA's Key Principles of Governance
Apply SAMA's fit and proper criteria and non-objection rule for senior positions
Handle a violation report under SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy, protecting the reporter and following the processing stages
Plan training under paragraph 72 and assemble the evidence a SAMA review expects

quest.name: The Compliance Charter
quest.premise: You have just joined Durrah Bank, a fictional conventional bank headquartered in Riyadh with branches in Jeddah and Al-Khobar, as a Compliance Officer. A fee has been charged that SAMA's rules do not allow, a new director wants to start before SAMA's letter arrives, and a branch employee has just blown the whistle. With Chief Compliance Officer Hind Al-Subaie, board secretary Turki Al-Mutlaq, audit head Grace Mwangi, branch manager Khalid Al-Ghamdi and reports officer Dana Al-Shehri, clear five stages, then face the final boss: SAMA's review.

sessions.title: SAMA's Principles of Compliance: Compliance Starts at the Top
sessions.summary: Meet SAMA's Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks (2020): what non-compliance risk is, how the board, senior management and the compliance unit share the work, the yearly cycle of risk assessment, reporting and the annual compliance report, and why every employee owns compliance.
objectives: Explain what SAMA means by compliance risk and the areas its compliance principles cover
Distinguish the compliance duties of the board, senior management and the compliance unit
Describe the yearly cycle of risk assessment, board reporting and the annual compliance report to SAMA
Recognise when a compliance failure must be escalated to the board and to SAMA at once

cards.title: Day one in the Compliance Division
cards.setting: Durrah Bank head office, King Fahd Road, Riyadh. Sunday morning.

lines.text: You join Durrah Bank, a fictional conventional bank, as a new Compliance Officer. Chief Compliance Officer Hind Al-Subaie meets you at the lift.
Welcome. Before you get a laptop, you get this: SAMA's Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks. Our policy is built on them.
And the board will ask you about them. The annual compliance report goes to the board before it goes to SAMA.
Turki is our Board Secretary and Director of Governance. He keeps us honest about deadlines.
Hind, quick one from Al-Khobar: a product team wants to launch a new card next month. Do they still need us?
They do, and so does every team. Compliance is not a department. It is everyone's job, starting with the board.
Your quest has five stages. Stage one: the Compliance Charter. Who owns compliance at a Saudi bank?

cards.title: SAMA's compliance principles in six scenes

scenes.heading: The instrument
scenes.narration: SAMA issued its Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks in September 2020, updating the older compliance manual for banks. They set a minimum, and SAMA expects better practice where possible.

scenes.heading: Who they cover
scenes.narration: Local commercial banks and branches of foreign banks licensed in the Kingdom, including their branches and offices abroad unless local law conflicts.

scenes.heading: Compliance risk
scenes.narration: The risk of regulatory penalties, serious financial loss or reputational damage because the bank fails to follow laws, SAMA instructions, or ethical and conduct standards.

scenes.heading: Tone from the top
scenes.narration: Compliance starts with the chairman, the board and senior management, who should lead by example.

scenes.heading: Everyone's job
scenes.narration: Compliance is part of the bank's culture and not limited to the compliance unit. Each employee carries responsibility for it.

scenes.heading: Three layers
scenes.narration: The board approves the policy and oversees, senior management manages the risk, and the compliance unit coordinates, advises, monitors and reports.

cards.title: Governance of compliance at a Saudi bank

items.label: Board of directors
items.detail: Approves the compliance policy, oversees non-compliance risk, evaluates effectiveness at least yearly.

items.label: Senior management
items.detail: Owns and manages non-compliance risk; prepares the policy, applies sanctions, reports to the board.

items.label: Compliance unit
items.detail: Independent unit led by the Chief Compliance Officer: advises, monitors, tests and reports.

items.label: Every employee
items.detail: First line of defence: knows the rules for their job and reports violations.

cards.caption: Built from the governance framework described in the introduction to SAMA's compliance principles (paragraph 22).

cards.question: Under SAMA's compliance principles, who bears the responsibility for effectively managing non-compliance risk in a local bank?
options: The compliance unit, because it is the expert function
Senior management, with the compliance unit assisting it
The internal audit unit, through its periodic reviews
Each business unit alone, without central coordination
cards.explanation: Principle 2 places responsibility for managing non-compliance risk on senior management. The compliance unit helps through advice, monitoring and oversight, and the board oversees. Internal audit reviews compliance; it does not manage it.

cards.title: What 'compliance' covers in SAMA's eyes
Board or senior management?
cards.prompt: Sort each duty to the party SAMA's compliance principles give it to in a local bank.

items.text: Approve the compliance policy and its updates
Evaluate the effectiveness of non-compliance risk management at least once a year
Approve the annual compliance report and give SAMA a copy
Prepare and update the compliance policy and communicate it to all sectors
Make sure corrective and disciplinary action follows policy breaches
Identify the main non-compliance risks and plan how to manage them at least annually
Commit to giving the compliance unit adequate resources on a continuing basis
Build and develop a permanent, independent compliance unit

cards.title: The silent quarter
cards.setting: Durrah Bank, executive floor. Wednesday afternoon.

lines.text: Hind, my audit team found something. Retail has been charging a fee SAMA's instructions do not allow. It started three months ago.
How many customers?
Thousands, across all regions. Retail says they planned to mention it in the year-end report.
Year-end? The board meets in five months.
This cannot wait for a routine report. Let's look at what the principles say about significant failures.

cards.title: A significant failure, discovered mid-year
cards.situation: Internal audit has found that a retail fee breaching SAMA instructions has been charged to thousands of customers for three months. The head of retail wants to fix the system quietly, refund customers next quarter and include the matter in the annual compliance report. You are drafting Hind's next step.

choices.text: Report it in writing to the board (or its delegated committee) straight away, start correction and refunds, and assess with Hind whether SAMA must be told directly.
choices.outcome: Best. Senior management, helped by compliance, must report significant failures to the board immediately and in writing. Where the impact could reach the banking sector's reputation, the Chief Compliance Officer must also notify SAMA directly and promptly.

choices.text: Accept the retail plan, but log the issue in the compliance unit's register so it appears in the annual report.
choices.outcome: Partly right: logging matters, but a failure that can lead to penalties and reputational harm must reach the board immediately, not at year end.

choices.text: Tell retail to fix it and leave reporting to internal audit, since audit found the issue.
choices.outcome: Poor. Audit informs the head of compliance of its findings, but reporting significant compliance failures to the board is a senior management and compliance duty, not something to hand back to audit.

choices.text: Wait until the fee is fully refunded so the board receives a closed issue rather than an open one.
choices.outcome: Poor. Delaying escalation to present a tidy picture defeats the purpose. The board must decide with accurate information while the problem is live.

cards.title: Durrah Bank's yearly compliance cycle

items.label: Assess the risks
items.detail: Senior management, with compliance, identifies the main non-compliance risks and plans, at least annually.

items.label: Monitor and test
items.detail: The compliance unit monitors and tests compliance continuously, with representative tests.

items.label: Report in writing
items.detail: Written reports to the board or its committee at least annually; significant failures at once.

items.label: Board evaluates
items.detail: The board or a delegated committee evaluates effectiveness at least once a year.

items.label: Annual report to SAMA
items.detail: Board-approved annual compliance report sent to SAMA by the end of April, signed off by the chairman.

cards.caption: Paragraphs 33, 35, 39, 76 and 80 of SAMA's compliance principles.

cards.back: An independent function at the first managerial level that identifies, assesses, advises on, monitors and reports on non-compliance risk.
The unit whose head and staff do only compliance work, at group, sector or department level depending on the bank's structure.
An employee in another business unit whom the Chief Compliance Officer designates to handle set compliance tasks in that unit.
The board-approved policy setting compliance responsibilities, the unit's authority and the bank's method for managing compliance risk.
Everything SAMA issues as regulator: regulations, rules, principles, frameworks, guides and mandatory circulars.
When a compliance person has an interest or relationship in a matter they review that could stop, or seem to stop, an impartial decision.

cards.question: By when must SAMA receive Durrah Bank's board-approved annual compliance report?
options: Within ten working days of the board meeting
By the end of April each year
Together with the audited financial statements
By the end of the first quarter of each year
cards.explanation: Paragraph 80 says SAMA should receive the board-approved annual compliance report by the end of April each year, sent by the chairman of a local bank (or the head of a foreign bank branch), as part of the bank's compliance self-assessment.

cards.title: Real cases: when compliance risk becomes a SAMA penalty (2017 and 2020)
cards.body:
SAMA's own statements show how breaches of its instructions turn into penalties and public naming.

- **September 2017:** SAMA said it had established that the **National Commercial Bank** deducted more from customers' salaries than the percentages its rules allow. SAMA fined the bank, pointed out the violation and required corrective action.
- **November 2020:** SAMA announced penalty decisions against **30 financial institutions**, several banks among them, for breaching its principles of responsible financing for individuals (the share of a customer's monthly income taken by credit obligations). It ordered corrections, published the list of names and said it could stop an institution offering the product if violations continued.

**The compliance lesson:** each case began as a business practice that drifted from a SAMA instruction. Monitoring, testing and escalation are how a bank catches drift before the regulator does.

*Sources: SAMA news statements of 12 September 2017 and 24 November 2020.*

cards.title: Who fixes, who advises?

items.label: Correcting a deficiency
items.left: Head of the unit where it occurred

items.label: Explaining a new SAMA instruction
items.left: Applies it in policies and processes

items.label: Compliance policy
items.right: Helps draft and keeps it current

cards.caption: Paragraphs 29, 63 and 64: the compliance unit supports; it does not take ownership away from the business.

cards.title: Compliance Charter take-aways
items: SAMA's Principles of Compliance (2020) apply to local commercial banks and foreign bank branches in the Kingdom and set a minimum standard.
Compliance risk covers penalties, financial loss and reputational damage, including from breaches of ethical and conduct codes.
The board approves the policy and evaluates effectiveness at least yearly; senior management manages the risk; the compliance unit coordinates and advises.
Significant failures go to the board in writing immediately, and to SAMA directly when the sector's reputation is at stake.
The board-approved annual compliance report reaches SAMA by the end of April each year.

cards.prompt: Think of one rule that applies to your own job. Who in your bank owns compliance with it, who checks it, and who would tell the board if it broke down?

quiz.question: Which institutions do SAMA's Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks apply to?
options: Only local commercial banks listed on the Saudi stock exchange
Only foreign bank branches, since local banks have separate governance rules
Local commercial banks and foreign bank branches licensed in the Kingdom, including their branches and offices abroad
All institutions SAMA supervises, including insurers and finance companies
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 30 applies the principles to all commercial banks in the Kingdom and their foreign branches and offices, unless host-country law conflicts. Insurers and finance companies are not the subject of this instrument.

quiz.question: A business head says compliance is 'the compliance team's problem'. Which statement in SAMA's principles contradicts this most directly?
options: Compliance staff must sign off every customer transaction
Only the board may decide which rules the bank applies
Business heads may delegate compliance entirely to compliance officers
Each individual in the bank carries responsibility for compliance, which must be part of the bank's culture
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 20 says compliance is part of the culture and not limited to the compliance unit; every individual carries responsibility. The other options are not in the principles.

quiz.question: Under the principles, how often must the board or a delegated committee evaluate the effectiveness of the bank's non-compliance risk management?
options: Every quarter, at each regular board meeting
Only when SAMA requests it after an inspection
At least once a year
Every three years, alongside the external review
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 33 requires the board, or a committee it delegates, to evaluate the effectiveness of non-compliance risk management at least once a year.

quiz.question: Durrah Bank's compliance unit finds a failure that could bring heavy regulatory penalties. What do the principles require?
options: Inform the business head and close the matter once fixed
Report it in writing to the board or its delegated committee immediately
Wait for internal audit to confirm it before reporting
Include it in the next annual compliance report
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 39 requires immediate written reporting to the board or its delegated committee of significant failures or violations, and paragraph 78 repeats this. Waiting for the annual report or for audit is too late.

quiz.question: When must the Chief Compliance Officer notify SAMA directly and promptly?
options: On strong indicators of significant compliance failures that affect the banking sector's reputation
Only after the board has approved the notification
Every quarter, with a summary of all minor findings
Whenever any customer complaint is upheld by the bank
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 59 requires the CCO to notify SAMA's bank supervision promptly and directly on strong indicators of significant or serious failures affecting the sector's reputation. Board approval is not a precondition.

quiz.question: Which body approves Durrah Bank's compliance policy?
options: The board of directors
SAMA's bank supervision department
The internal audit unit
The Chief Compliance Officer
quiz.explanation: Principle 1 makes the board responsible for approving and overseeing an effective compliance policy, prepared by senior management (Principle 3). For a foreign bank branch, the branch's chief officer takes the board's role.

quiz.question: A product manager argues that a practice is legal, so reputational concerns raised by compliance are irrelevant. Which point from SAMA's principles best answers him?
options: The bank must weigh actions that could provoke strong negative reactions and harm its reputation even without an actual violation
Reputation is a matter for marketing, not for compliance
Only written SAMA instructions can be considered by compliance
Compliance may veto any product it considers unpopular
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 20 asks the bank to consider the impact of its actions on shareholders, customers, employees and the market that could damage reputation even if no rule is broken. Compliance advises; it does not hold a general veto.

quiz.question: Who sends the board-approved annual compliance report of a local bank to SAMA?
options: The chief financial officer
The chairman of the board
The head of internal audit
The Chief Compliance Officer
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 80 says the chairman of a local bank (or the chief of a foreign bank branch) sends the board-approved report to SAMA by the end of April each year.

quiz.question: Which of these is listed among the topics that compliance rules and standards cover under SAMA's principles?
options: Approving the annual marketing budget
Setting the bank's dividend policy
Choosing the bank's external auditor
Handling reports of violations
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 24 lists fair market practice, conflicts of interest, fair treatment, suitable advice, AML/CTF, KYC, fraud, corruption and handling reports of violations. The others are not compliance topics in the principles.

quiz.question: Senior management at Durrah Bank discovers that a manager breached the compliance policy. What duty do the principles give senior management?
options: Refer the matter to SAMA for a decision on discipline
Make sure appropriate corrective and disciplinary action is taken
Leave discipline to the compliance unit
Record it and act only if it happens again
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 38 gives senior management the duty to ensure adherence to the compliance policy and that corrective and disciplinary action follows any violation.

sessions.title: An Independent, Resourced Compliance Function
sessions.summary: Inside SAMA's compliance unit principles: the four elements of independence, the Chief Compliance Officer's level, reporting line and rights, SAMA's non-objection, pay rules, resources and training, the unit's duties from new circulars to testing and reporting, its separation from internal audit, and limits on delegation.
objectives: Explain the four elements of compliance independence and the Chief Compliance Officer's reporting line
Apply the rules on SAMA non-objection, conflicts of interest and remuneration for compliance staff
Describe the compliance unit's duties: communicating instructions, approving new products, monitoring, testing and reporting
Distinguish the roles of the compliance unit and internal audit and the limits on delegating compliance tasks

lines.text: The CEO wants a leaner chart. One idea: compliance reports to the Chief Operating Officer, and Hind also takes over branch operations.
Branch operations? Then I would be checking my own work.
And pay? HR suggested linking compliance bonuses to retail revenue so everyone 'pulls in the same direction'.
Three problems in one proposal. Turki, can you get us ten minutes with the CEO?
Yes. Bring the principles. He respects paragraph numbers.
Stage two: the Independent Desk. Let's find out what independence really means.

scenes.heading: Official status
scenes.narration: The compliance unit has a formal standing, written into the compliance policy or a related document, and all staff are told about it.

scenes.heading: A senior head
scenes.narration: In a local bank the unit is headed by an executive at the first managerial level, with overall responsibility for coordinating compliance risk management.

scenes.heading: No conflicting roles
scenes.narration: Compliance staff, and above all the head of compliance, must not hold other duties that could conflict with their compliance work.

scenes.heading: Free access
scenes.narration: Every compliance staff member may access any relevant information, record or file and speak to any employee needed to do the job.

scenes.heading: Not isolation
scenes.narration: Independence means freedom from interference, not distance. The unit should work closely with the business to spot risks early.

cards.title: Independence: what it means and what it does not

items.label: Reporting line
items.left: CCO reports to the CEO only
items.right: Not via the COO or a business head

items.label: Pay
items.left: May reflect the whole bank's results
items.right: Not tied to the business line checked

items.label: Board contact
items.left: Direct access to the board or committee

items.label: Cooperation
items.right: Is not a silo that avoids them

cards.caption: Paragraphs 45, 50, 57, 58 and 59 of SAMA's compliance principles.

cards.question: Under SAMA's principles, to whom should the Chief Compliance Officer of a local bank report administratively?
options: The chief operating officer
The chair of the audit committee
The CEO or managing director only
The head of risk management
cards.explanation: Paragraph 50 links the first-level compliance officer directly to the chief executive only (CEO, managing director or general manager). Paragraph 59 adds a right of direct access to the board or its delegated committee.

cards.title: The CCO's rights and duties
cards.prompt: Match each point to what SAMA's compliance principles say about it.

pairs.right: May communicate directly with the board or its committee, bypassing usual lines when needed.
Meets the board or its delegated committee at least once a year.
May investigate possible breaches and call on legal, audit or external experts.
Needs SAMA's non-objection, and so does the CCO leaving the post.
May delegate tasks, but stays accountable for all compliance work.
May hold regular, documented meetings with senior management and business heads.

cards.title: Pay, conflicts and who appoints
cards.body:
SAMA protects compliance independence through people rules as well as structure:

- **Only compliance work.** The CCO and compliance unit staff hold only compliance responsibilities (paragraph 57). Compliance officers placed in other units must avoid and disclose conflicts.
- **Pay.** Rewards must not depend on the financial performance of the business the person checks. They may reflect the bank's overall results, and the **board or a board committee** gives final approval (paragraph 58).
- **Appointment.** Choosing the head and staff of compliance follows SAMA's Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions. The head of compliance selects the unit's staff (paragraph 43).
- **Changes.** The board is told of any appointment or change of CCO, with reasons; SAMA's **non-objection** is needed for the appointment and when the CCO leaves the post (paragraphs 51-52).
- **Reporting lines.** All compliance unit staff report to the CCO. Compliance officers in other units keep a mandatory compliance line to the CCO, which prevails (paragraph 54).

lines.text: The cards team has already emailed SAMA asking for approval of the new travel card. They said compliance would slow them down.
Who signed the email?
The product director. They also signed with an outsourced call centre for card activation.
Did compliance see the outsourcing contract?
Nobody asked.
Two principles skipped in one afternoon. Let's decide how to put this right.

cards.title: The product team went straight to SAMA
cards.situation: Durrah Bank's cards team sent its own request to SAMA for approval of a new card without compliance review. It also signed an outsourcing agreement for card activation without involving compliance. The launch date is in three weeks and the CEO is keen to keep it.

choices.text: Ask the product director to withdraw the request, review the product and the outsourcing deal, then let the CCO submit a single request to SAMA; report the process breach to senior management.
choices.outcome: Best. Paragraph 66 requires compliance approval before any request to SAMA for a new product, and only the CCO submits such requests. Paragraph 67 requires compliance to take part in decisions to assign work to third parties. Reporting the breach lets senior management correct the process.

choices.text: Let the request stand to save time, and review the product in parallel while SAMA considers it.
choices.outcome: Partly right: reviewing helps, but the request reached SAMA through the wrong channel and without compliance approval. Repairing the route matters as much as the content.

choices.text: Approve the product informally by email so the record shows compliance agreed.
choices.outcome: Poor. Backdating approval hides a control failure and still leaves the request with SAMA from the wrong sender.

choices.text: Leave it: product approvals are the business's responsibility, not compliance's.
choices.outcome: Poor. The principles give compliance an explicit gatekeeping role for new products and for outsourcing decisions.

cards.title: What the compliance unit does all year

items.label: Communicate
items.detail: Pass new laws and SAMA instructions to senior management and units promptly; keep a database.

items.label: Identify and measure
items.detail: Spot compliance risks in new products and practices; use indicators such as complaints and fraud cases.

items.label: Monitor and test
items.detail: Continuous monitoring with adequate, representative compliance tests.

items.label: Report
items.detail: Regular written CCO reports to senior management: risks, changes, breaches, fixes and dates.

items.label: Advise and train
items.detail: Answer staff questions and help senior management run awareness and training.

cards.caption: Principle 7, paragraphs 63-86, in five steps.

cards.title: From a new SAMA circular to daily practice
cards.prompt: Put the compliance unit's steps for a new SAMA instruction in order, as paragraphs 29 and 65 describe them.
steps: Receive the new circular from SAMA
Record it in the compliance database that all staff can use
Explain it promptly to senior management and the business units concerned
Obtain the units' confirmation that they have received and understood it
Check the requirement is built into policies, procedures and products
Monitor and test that it is applied, and report gaps

cards.back: No. Principle 8 requires the two to be separate and independent within the bank.
Internal audit periodically reviews the compliance unit's activities and the bank's compliance risks.
Compliance identifies the rules, builds them into policy and checks they work; audit tests controls across all units by sampling or full review.
Internal audit informs the head of compliance of audit findings that relate to compliance.
The compliance unit also checks that internal audit carries out what SAMA requires of it, in the set manner and time.

cards.question: Durrah Bank wants to outsource part of its compliance testing to a consultancy. What do the principles require?
options: Nothing, provided the consultancy is a licensed audit firm
Board approval only, as delegation is an internal matter
Internal audit must take over responsibility for the outsourced work
SAMA's non-objection before the agreement, with the CCO still responsible
cards.explanation: Principle 10 allows some activities to be delegated, but they remain under the CCO's supervision and responsibility, the arrangement must not hinder supervision, and SAMA's non-objection is needed before entering any delegation agreement.

cards.title: Red flags the compliance programme must watch
Independent Desk take-aways
items: Independence has four elements: official status, a first-level head, no conflicting roles, and free access to information and people.
The CCO reports to the CEO only, holds no business duties, meets the board at least yearly and can go to the board or SAMA directly.
SAMA's non-objection is needed to appoint the CCO and when the CCO leaves; compliance pay must not depend on the business line checked.
New product requests reach SAMA only through the CCO after compliance approval; compliance takes part in outsourcing decisions.
Compliance and internal audit stay separate; audit reviews compliance, and delegating compliance work needs SAMA's non-objection.

cards.prompt: Look at how your bank's compliance unit is set up. Which of the four elements of independence is strongest, and which would you want to strengthen first?

quiz.question: Which of these is one of the four elements of compliance independence in SAMA's principles?
options: All compliance staff can access relevant information and records and talk to employees as needed
The compliance unit approves the bank's annual budget
Compliance staff are chosen by the business units they monitor
The compliance unit reports to the external auditor
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 46 lists official status, a first-level head, no conflicts of interest, and the right to access information and communicate with staff. The other options are not elements of independence.

quiz.question: HR proposes that compliance staff bonuses depend on the retail division's profits. What do the principles say?
options: Compliance staff may not receive any performance-related reward
Linking bonuses to retail profit is fine if the CEO approves it
Bonus rules for compliance are for HR alone to decide
Rewards must not be tied to the performance of the business the staff check, and the board or its committee gives final approval
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 58 forbids tying compliance rewards to the business line they monitor, allows links to the bank's overall performance, and requires final approval by the board or a board committee.

quiz.question: Durrah Bank's CCO resigns. What does SAMA require in addition to informing the board?
options: Nothing further, as departures are an internal matter
Only a notice in the bank's next annual report
Approval from the bank's general assembly
SAMA's non-objection to the departure, with documentation and reasons
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 52 requires SAMA's non-objection for the CCO's appointment and also when the CCO leaves the post, with documents and reasons. Paragraph 51 requires the board to be told.

quiz.question: The CEO asks Hind to also lead branch operations to save a salary. Why is this a problem under the principles?
options: It is allowed if the board records the decision in its minutes
The CCO and compliance staff should hold only compliance responsibilities, with no banking activity duties
It is a problem only if the CCO's pay rises as a result
It is allowed for one year while a replacement is found
quiz.explanation: Paragraphs 50 and 57 say the CCO must not hold direct or indirect responsibility for banking activities, and compliance staff hold only compliance duties, to protect independence.

quiz.question: A compliance officer works inside the Treasury unit. Which reporting line prevails for compliance matters?
options: The line to the internal audit unit
The line to the head of Treasury only
The line to the Chief Compliance Officer, which is controlling and mandatory
Whichever manager is more senior
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 54 says compliance officers in other units have a functional line to their unit but a compliance line to the CCO; to avoid dual hierarchy, the line to the CCO is controlling and mandatory.

quiz.question: Who may submit a request to SAMA for approval of a new product at Durrah Bank?
options: Only the Chief Compliance Officer, after compliance approval
Any senior executive with the CEO's consent
The head of the business unit that owns the product
The board secretary on behalf of the board
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 66 requires business units to obtain compliance approval first, and requests for SAMA approval or non-objection are submitted only by the CCO.

quiz.question: How often must the CCO meet the board or its delegated committee under the principles?
options: At least once a year
Only when a significant failure occurs
Every two years, at the board evaluation
At every board meeting
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 59 says the CCO should meet the board or its delegated committee at least once a year to help it assess the bank's management of non-compliance risk.

quiz.question: A business head says compliance should fix the gap it found in his unit's procedure. What does paragraph 64 say?
options: Internal audit decides who fixes it
Senior management and the unit's head correct it; compliance advises, follows up and reports any shortfall
Compliance must rewrite the procedure itself within a month
The board must approve every correction before work starts
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 64 places correction on senior management and the heads of the units concerned. Compliance's role is limited to advice, follow-up and reporting failures to correct.

quiz.question: Which statement about the compliance unit and internal audit is correct?
options: They may be merged in smaller banks to save cost
They must be separate and independent, and internal audit periodically reviews compliance
Compliance reviews internal audit's work and not the other way round
Internal audit approves the compliance programme each year
quiz.explanation: Principle 8 requires the two units to be separate and independent, with internal audit reviewing the compliance unit's activities periodically. Compliance also checks audit meets SAMA's requirements, but that does not replace audit's review.

quiz.question: A bank misreads a SAMA circular and applies it wrongly. According to paragraph 65, what follows?
options: SAMA must reissue the circular before taking any action
The penalty is waived if the bank acted in good faith
The bank is not exempt from regulatory penalties because of the incorrect application
Only the employee who misread it can be penalised
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 65 stresses understanding instructions and seeking clarification from compliance or SAMA if needed, because incorrect application does not exempt the bank from penalties.

sessions.title: Board Governance, Committees and Senior Appointments
sessions.summary: SAMA's Key Principles of Governance (version 2, 2024): board qualifications, size and independence, the induction every member receives, meetings, the board's duties towards control functions, and the executive, audit, nomination and remuneration, and risk committees. Then the fit and proper rules and SAMA non-objection for senior positions, and a real governance penalty.
objectives: Describe the board qualifications, composition and independence tests in SAMA's Key Principles of Governance
Explain the induction programme each board member must receive and the board's duties towards control functions
Compare the make-up and roles of the four main board committees
Apply SAMA's fit and proper criteria and the non-objection rule for senior positions

cards.title: A new face at the board table
cards.setting: Durrah Bank boardroom, 22nd floor. Tuesday evening.

lines.text: The general assembly elected Dr Nasser last month. The chairman wants him on the audit committee at Thursday's meeting.
Has SAMA's no-objection letter arrived?
Not yet. And he has not had his induction either.
There's more. His wife holds a SAR 3 million finance facility with us. Is he still independent?
The chairman says it's a formality.
In governance, formalities are the point. Stage three: the Boardroom.

scenes.heading: One rulebook for boards
scenes.narration: SAMA's Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions set minimum governance requirements. Version 2 was issued in May 2024.

scenes.heading: Mandatory for banks
scenes.narration: They apply on a mandatory basis to local banks, finance companies and real estate refinancing companies, and as guidance to several other licensed sectors.

scenes.heading: Chair and CEO apart
scenes.narration: Effective governance needs the roles of board chairman and chief executive to be separate, with clear powers for each.

scenes.heading: A control framework
scenes.narration: The board relies on risk management, internal audit and compliance departments, internal controls and an external auditor.

scenes.heading: Seven principles
scenes.narration: Board qualifications; formation and board affairs; board duties; executive management duties; committees; shareholder rights; disclosure and transparency.

cards.title: Board numbers in the Key Principles

items.label: Board size
items.detail: Any covered institution: 5 to 11 members. Banks: 9 to 11 as best practice.

items.label: Independent members
items.detail: At least two members or one third of the board, whichever is greater.

items.label: Executive members
items.detail: No more than two executive members on the board.

items.label: Board meetings
items.detail: At least four a year, one every three months, plus extra meetings when needed.

items.label: Term of office
items.detail: Elected by the general assembly for a term of no more than three years; re-election allowed.

cards.caption: Principle 2, paragraphs 7, 8 and 22, with the footnote for banks.

cards.question: What must every new Durrah Bank board member receive under paragraph 19 of the Key Principles of Governance?
options: A copy of the bank's audited accounts for the last five years
An induction programme on the bank's mission, strategy and activities, with a memorandum on the duties of membership
A certificate from SAMA confirming they passed a governance examination
A meeting with the external auditor before their first board meeting
cards.explanation: Paragraph 19 requires an induction programme explaining the institution's mission, strategic objectives and activities, plus a memorandum explaining the duties and responsibilities of membership.

cards.title: Independent or not?
cards.prompt: Using the definition of an independent member in the Key Principles, sort each board candidate.

items.text: Holds 6% of the bank's shares
Worked for the bank's external auditor until last year
Has served 10 years in total on the bank's board
Spouse holds a SAR 3 million credit facility with the bank
Is the brother of a senior executive of the bank
Retired professor with no shares, ties or contracts with the bank
Holds a small personal account and no credit with the bank
Sits on the board of an unrelated manufacturing company

cards.title: Four board committees
cards.prompt: Match each committee to a rule the Key Principles set for it.

pairs.right: Three to five members, may not be chaired by the CEO, at least six meetings a year.
For banks all members independent; chaired by an independent member, never by the board chairman.
At least two independent members; proposes board and executive candidates and the pay policy.
Members know risk management and include an expert in cyber and technical risk.
A member should preferably sit on no more than two committees.

cards.title: Induction, learning and the control functions
cards.body:
The Key Principles treat board knowledge as a duty, not a courtesy:

- **Competence** includes education, experience and a **willingness to keep learning**; members need financial literacy to read statements and ratios (paragraph 5).
- **Induction** for every member on the bank's mission, strategy and activities, with a written memorandum of duties (paragraph 19).
- Members must **know the rules and instructions** that apply to the bank and keep up with changes (paragraph 21), and develop their knowledge of its activities (paragraph 6).
- The board must make sure **compliance, internal audit and risk management** exist, are independent from business units, have enough powers and resources, and that their **staff are trained** (paragraph 36).
- The board approves policies on conduct and ethics, on **reporting violations and protecting whistleblowers**, on complaints and on confidentiality (paragraph 46).
- The board tells SAMA in writing of penalties from any authority that may affect the bank within **ten working days** (paragraph 40).

cards.title: Real case: SAMA fines Banque Saudi Fransi over governance failings (2017)
cards.body:
In **October 2017** SAMA issued a statement that it was following the steps the board of **Banque Saudi Fransi** had taken to address deficiencies in applying sound governance and control policies.

In **November 2017** SAMA added details. After receiving information about an employee incentives programme for past years, it sent **inspectors** to verify it and review the bank's policies, controls and authority manual. It held several meetings with the board, which took urgent decisions: appointing an **independent examination team** reporting to SAMA and the board, **stopping the incentives programme**, reviewing the authority table, changing the organisation structure and making new management appointments. The bank was filing court cases to recover amounts paid outside the programme or the powers granted.

SAMA found the bank had committed violations of sound governance and supervisory policies and **imposed fines**, and passed matters outside its remit to the competent authorities.

*Sources: SAMA statements of 11 October and 23 November 2017.*

cards.title: Start on Thursday?
cards.situation: The chairman wants Dr Nasser to join Thursday's audit committee meeting and be named in a press release. SAMA's written non-objection for his board and committee membership has not yet arrived, and his independence questionnaire shows that his wife holds a SAR 3 million finance facility with the bank.

choices.text: Advise the chairman that Dr Nasser cannot act or be announced until SAMA's non-objection arrives, and that the facility above SAR 1 million means he cannot be treated as independent for audit committee purposes.
choices.outcome: Best. SAMA's non-objection must come before nomination to the board and committees, and the senior appointments rules bar candidates from taking up roles or announcing them first. A credit relationship above SAR 1 million in a relative's name removes independence, and a bank's audit committee must be fully independent.

choices.text: Let him attend as an observer without voting, and hold the press release until the letter arrives.
choices.outcome: Partly right on the announcement, but sitting in a committee before non-objection still risks him exercising the role. The independence problem also remains unaddressed.

choices.text: Let him attend and vote, then send SAMA the papers afterwards, since the general assembly has already elected him.
choices.outcome: Poor. Election by the general assembly does not replace SAMA's prior written non-objection.

choices.text: Ask the external auditor to confirm his independence instead of applying the bank's own test.
choices.outcome: Poor. The definition of independence is set in the Key Principles, and the board is responsible for applying it each year.

cards.title: Filling a senior position at Durrah Bank

items.label: Policy and assessment
items.detail: Board-approved fit and proper policy; the bank assesses the candidate and checks certificates.

items.label: Tell the candidate
items.detail: Job offers state that the post needs SAMA's written non-objection.

items.label: Request non-objection
items.detail: Bank sends SAMA the fit and proper form, assessment results and required documents.

items.label: Wait for SAMA
items.detail: No starting, acting or announcing until SAMA's written non-objection arrives.

items.label: Reassess yearly
items.detail: Fit and proper reassessed at least annually; material concerns reported to SAMA at once.

items.label: Report changes
items.detail: Start dates, resignations and departures notified to SAMA within the time the rules set.

cards.caption: SAMA's Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions. The English page says it is not the latest version: check the Arabic text for current details.

cards.back: Personal honesty, fairness and good reputation; no conviction for a crime touching honour or integrity unless rehabilitated.
The qualifications or experience and skills for the role, and an understanding of the business, its risks and management.
Able to manage personal financial obligations prudently. It is about conduct, not the size of a person's wealth.
No interests, obligations or relationships that could create a conflict or impair independent performance of the role.
The bank's board must ensure candidates for senior positions are fit and proper, under the bank's own policy.
Board and committee members and listed senior posts, including the CEO, CFO, CRO, CCO, head of internal audit and AML director.

cards.question: Which statement about SAMA's Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions is correct?
options: Once SAMA gives non-objection, the bank never needs to reassess the person
The general assembly, not the board, is responsible for fit and proper checks
A candidate may start work while SAMA reviews the request if the CEO agrees
The bank must reassess the fitness and propriety of senior position holders at least annually
cards.explanation: The requirements ask the bank to assess senior position holders periodically and at least annually, and report material concerns to SAMA immediately. Candidates may not take up their roles before written non-objection, and the board is responsible for fit and proper assessments.

cards.title: Boardroom take-aways
items: SAMA's Key Principles of Governance (version 2, May 2024) are mandatory for local banks; the chair and CEO roles must be separate.
Banks should have 9 to 11 board members as best practice, at least a third independent, and no more than two executives; the board meets at least four times a year.
Every member receives an induction and a memorandum of duties, must know the applicable rules, and keeps learning.
The board ensures compliance, audit and risk functions are independent, resourced and trained, and approves the whistleblowing policy.
Board members and listed senior posts need SAMA's written non-objection before acting; fit and proper status is reassessed at least yearly.

cards.prompt: If you joined a board tomorrow, what would you want your induction to cover first, and what could you only learn by asking the control functions directly?

quiz.question: To which institutions do SAMA's Key Principles of Governance apply on a mandatory basis?
options: Only foreign bank branches licensed in the Kingdom
Only banks listed on the Saudi stock exchange
Local banks, finance companies and real estate refinancing companies
All companies registered in Saudi Arabia
quiz.explanation: Section 3 of the principles makes them mandatory for local banks, finance companies and real estate refinancing companies, and guidance for several other licensed sectors.

quiz.question: A Saudi bank's board has 11 members, 3 of them independent. Does this meet the independence rule?
options: No: a bank's board must be entirely independent
Yes: two independent members are always enough
No: at least one third of the board must be independent, so 4 are needed
Yes: independence rules apply only to committees
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7 requires at least two independent members or one third of the board, whichever is greater. One third of 11 is more than 3, so 4 independent members are needed.

quiz.question: What does the induction programme in paragraph 19 explain to a new board member?
options: The personal financial records of the other board members
The institution's mission, strategic objectives and activities, with a memorandum on the duties of membership
Only the bank's IT and cyber security architecture
SAMA's internal inspection manual and examination procedures
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 19 requires an induction programme on mission, strategic objectives and activities, plus a memorandum explaining the member's duties and responsibilities.

quiz.question: Who may chair a bank's audit committee under the Key Principles?
options: An independent member who is not the board chairman
The CEO, who knows the bank's operations best
The board chairman, to give the committee authority
The head of internal audit
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 78 requires the audit committee to be chaired by an independent member and not by the board chairman; for banks all members must be independent.

quiz.question: Which committee must include an expert in cyber and technical risks?
options: The risk committee
The executive committee
The nomination and remuneration committee
The audit committee
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 89 requires risk committee members to know risk management and to include an expert in cyber and technical risks.

quiz.question: Within what period must the board notify SAMA in writing of a penalty from another authority that may affect the bank's functioning?
options: Thirty days from the date of the penalty
Ten working days from the date of the penalty
In the next annual report
Five working days from the date of the penalty
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 40 requires written notice to SAMA within ten working days of any penalty from a supervisory, regulatory or judicial authority that may affect the institution's functioning.

quiz.question: A board member's son, a sole trader, has a SAR 1.5 million credit facility with the bank. What follows under the Key Principles?
options: The member cannot be classed as independent, as a relative's credit exceeds SAR 1 million
Nothing, because the facility is in the son's name
The facility must be cancelled before the next meeting
The member must resign from the board immediately
quiz.explanation: The independence definition lists a credit relationship above SAR 1,000,000 in the member's name or a relative's name. Children are relatives. It affects independence; it does not require resignation from the board.

quiz.question: Under SAMA's senior appointment requirements, which is one of the minimum fit and proper criteria?
options: Having worked at SAMA for at least five years
Financial soundness in handling personal financial obligations
Being a shareholder of the bank
Holding a minimum personal net worth
quiz.explanation: The four minimum criteria are honesty, integrity and reputation; competence and capability; financial soundness; and independence. Financial soundness is about prudence, not wealth.

quiz.question: A newly hired Chief Risk Officer wants to start next week while SAMA reviews the request. What is the rule?
options: He may start if the board approves an interim role
He may start but not sign documents for 30 days
He may start because the CRO is not a post that needs SAMA's non-objection
Candidates may not take up their role, act in it or announce it before SAMA's written non-objection
quiz.explanation: The requirements bar candidates for senior positions from assuming their duties or announcing the appointment before SAMA's written non-objection. The CRO is listed among bank posts needing it.

quiz.question: What did SAMA say it found at Banque Saudi Fransi in November 2017?
options: A failure to file suspicious transaction reports
Breaches of capital adequacy ratios
No violations, only weaknesses in customer service
Violations of sound governance and supervisory policies, for which it imposed fines
quiz.explanation: SAMA's statement of 23 November 2017 said that, after its inspection and the independent examination, the bank had committed violations of sound governance and supervisory policies, and SAMA imposed financial fines.

sessions.title: Speaking Up: SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions
sessions.summary: SAMA's 2019 Whistle Blowing Policy: who may report and what, the board-approved policy and the independent unit reporting to compliance, minimum reporting channels, confidentiality and protection from retaliation, the duties of whistleblowers and of the bank, the processing stages, automated reporting and performance indicators.
objectives: Explain the purpose, scope and key definitions of SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy
Describe the bank's general obligations, including the independent unit, the minimum channels and awareness programmes
Apply the duties of whistleblowers and the bank's duties on receiving a report, including confidentiality and protection
Order the processing stages and name what the automated system and performance indicators must show

cards.title: A message to the speak-up line
cards.setting: Durrah Bank, Violation Reports Unit, Riyadh. Sunday, 8:15.

lines.text: Hind, an email arrived overnight on the speak-up address. It says a procurement manager steered a contract to his brother-in-law's firm.
Who sent it?
It's signed by a branch employee in Al-Khobar. She attached two invoices.
I know her. She's nervous. She asked me if she'll lose her job for this.
Then our first job is to make sure she won't. Dana, log it and acknowledge receipt today.
Stage four: the Speak-Up Gate. SAMA has a policy for exactly this.

cards.title: SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy in five scenes

scenes.heading: Why it exists
scenes.narration: In August 2019 SAMA issued a policy setting the minimum controls for receiving and processing reports of violations, so that people can report without being harmed.

scenes.heading: Secure channels
scenes.narration: Its purpose is secure communication between whistleblowers and the units that handle reports, to fight fraud, embezzlement and corruption and unlawful, unethical or unprofessional conduct.

scenes.heading: Who it covers
scenes.narration: Banks, foreign bank branches, insurers, finance companies, finance lease registration companies and credit bureaus supervised by SAMA.

scenes.heading: Who may report
scenes.narration: Employees in the widest sense, from board and committee members to contract staff, consultants and third-party staff, and stakeholders such as customers and suppliers.

scenes.heading: What a violation is
scenes.narration: Any act or concealment of fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, misconduct, financial mismanagement, accounting irregularities, conflicts of interest or other breaches of laws and instructions.

cards.title: Processing stages every bank must define

items.label: Reception
items.detail: The report arrives through any channel and is logged.

items.label: Initial assessment
items.detail: Is it a violation within scope, and how serious is it?

items.label: Verification plan
items.detail: Decide how the facts will be checked and by whom.

items.label: Documented rationale
items.detail: Record the reasons supporting how the report is handled.

items.label: Decision
items.detail: Decide on the processing and any corrective action.

items.label: Follow-up
items.detail: Track that the decision is carried out.

items.label: Record keeping
items.detail: Keep reports and documents for the periods laws and instructions set.

cards.caption: Section III.g.5 of the policy: working procedures must name inputs, outputs, forms, systems and authorised people for each stage.

cards.question: Under SAMA's policy, to which department must the independent unit that receives and processes violation reports report?
options: Human resources
The compliance department
The business unit concerned
The external auditor
cards.explanation: Section III.b requires financial institutions to set up an independent administrative unit to receive and process violation reports and to report to the compliance department. SAMA's compliance principles also list handling violation reports among compliance's duties.

cards.title: Whose duty is it?
cards.prompt: Sort each duty under SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy.

items.text: Report as soon as possible, with the details and documents available
Avoid rumours and malicious reports meant to defame or take revenge
Keep the report confidential
Treat every report seriously, whatever its language or level of detail
Acknowledge receipt and, where possible, tell the reporter the decision
Refer the report to the unit responsible for control and investigation
Take corrective action if the violation is proven
Bear responsibility for malicious allegations that cause damage

cards.title: The bank's general obligations
cards.prompt: Match each element of the policy to what it requires of the bank.

pairs.right: A whistleblowing policy approved by the board of directors.
Periodic reports to the board and audit committee on cases received and actions taken.
A direct telephone number, a website, postal service and an email address.
Programmes that encourage staff and stakeholders to report and explain their responsibilities.
No action against a reporter whose good-faith claim is not proven in the investigation.
Only to competent authorities such as investigation and judicial bodies.

cards.title: The cold shoulder
cards.setting: Durrah Bank, Al-Khobar branch. Two weeks later.

lines.text: Hind, the procurement manager found out someone from my branch reported him. He's asking around who it was.
Nobody in my unit shared her name. But her supervisor has just moved her to the night shift.
The supervisor says it's routine rota planning.
Routine or not, the timing looks like retaliation. We need to act, and we need to be careful how.

cards.title: Protecting the reporter
cards.situation: The Al-Khobar employee who reported the procurement manager has been moved to night shifts two weeks after her report. The manager under investigation is asking colleagues who reported him. The investigation is not finished, and the evidence so far is mixed.

choices.text: Ask HR to pause the shift change pending review, remind the manager and supervisor in writing of the bank's duty to protect reporters and keep identities confidential, and log the events for the investigation.
choices.outcome: Best. The policy requires the bank to protect good-faith whistleblowers from retaliation by its employees and to keep their identity confidential at all stages. Acting quickly and recording the facts protects her and the integrity of the investigation.

choices.text: Wait for the investigation to finish: if the report is proven, then review the shift change.
choices.outcome: Partly right on keeping records, but protection does not depend on the report being proven. A good-faith report that is not established still attracts no action against the reporter.

choices.text: Tell the manager who made the report so he can answer her directly and settle the matter.
choices.outcome: Poor. The bank may disclose a whistleblower's identity only to competent authorities such as investigation and judicial bodies.

choices.text: Advise the employee to withdraw her report to avoid further trouble.
choices.outcome: Poor. This discourages reporting, which the policy requires the bank to encourage, and leaves the possible violation unaddressed.

cards.title: Good faith versus malicious reporting

items.label: Evidence
items.left: Real, reasonable information suggesting a violation
items.right: Rumours or claims with no basis

items.label: Aim
items.left: Correct errors, detect violations, protect values
items.right: Defame, take revenge or damage trust

cards.caption: Sections III.a, III.d and III.f of SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy.

cards.back: Fact: stakeholders such as shareholders, creditors, customers and suppliers are covered too.

cards.front: Myth: I need proof before I report.
cards.back: Fact: staff should not hold back just because they are unsure a report can be proven; real and reasonable information is enough to report.

cards.front: Myth: reports must be in Arabic and fully documented.
cards.back: Fact: the bank must treat every report seriously whatever its language, detail, impact or importance.

cards.front: Myth: only violations inside the bank count.
cards.back: Fact: the bank encourages reports of violations inside or outside it, within the scope of the reporter's work.

cards.front: Myth: anonymous reporters get the same protection claim.
cards.back: Fact: a reporter whose identity was not revealed and could not be discovered cannot claim protection from retaliation, as no one could target them.

cards.front: Myth: whistleblowing is only about fraud.
cards.back: Fact: the cases include misuse of assets, abuse of power, conflicts of interest, leaks of confidential data, safety risks and serious negligence.

cards.question: Which information must the bank's automated whistleblowing system be able to show, at a minimum?
options: The names of all reporters, sorted by department
Each reporter's performance rating and salary grade
The channel used, the total reports, reports by subject, reports processed and in progress, and the type of processing
Only the reports that were proven after investigation
cards.explanation: Section III.g.4 requires an automated system showing at least the receiving channel, total reports, reports by subject, numbers processed and in progress, and the type of processing, able to produce reports SAMA requests.

cards.title: Real case: SAMA announces the whistleblowing policy (2019)
cards.body:
On **7 August 2019** SAMA announced that it had issued a policy document on reporting violations at financial institutions operating in the Kingdom.

SAMA said the document sets the **minimum controls** for receiving and processing reports, so that employees of financial institutions and stakeholders can report violations easily and **without any negative impact** on them. Its aim, SAMA said, was secure channels between reporters and the higher management of financial institutions for violations committed or about to be committed, to combat **fraud, embezzlement and corruption**.

The policy itself gave institutions **three months** to implement it and asked them to give SAMA a **compliance plan within one month**.

**Lesson for you:** the policy is a supervisory requirement with a timeline, not a poster. A SAMA review can ask for the board approval, the unit's set-up, the channels, the case statistics and the awareness programme.

*Sources: SAMA news statement of 7 August 2019; Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions, SAMA Rulebook.*

cards.title: Speak-Up Gate take-aways
items: SAMA's 2019 policy sets minimum controls so employees and stakeholders can report violations without being harmed.
Each bank needs a board-approved policy, an independent reports unit reporting to compliance, and periodic reports to the board and audit committee.
Minimum channels are a direct phone line, a website, post and email, backed by awareness programmes that encourage reporting.
Identity and content stay confidential at every stage; good-faith reporters are protected, malicious reporters bear responsibility.
Reports go through defined stages from reception to record keeping, tracked by an automated system and performance indicators.

cards.prompt: Would a colleague in your team know how to report a violation today, and would they trust that nothing bad would happen to them? What would make the difference?

quiz.question: What is the stated objective of SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy?
options: To let customers complain directly to SAMA about service quality
To set the penalties SAMA imposes on employees who commit fraud
To set the minimum controls for receiving and processing reports so people can report without being negatively affected
To replace suspicious transaction reporting to the Financial Intelligence Unit
quiz.explanation: Section I.b says the policy provides the minimum controls to receive and process reports so that employees and stakeholders can report violations without being negatively affected.

quiz.question: Which of these people counts as a 'financial institution employee' under the policy?
options: A supplier's sales representative
A consultant working for the bank through a third-party firm
A shareholder with 2% of the bank's shares
A customer who holds a savings account
quiz.explanation: The definition covers board and committee members, executives, permanent and contract staff, consultants and people working through a third party. Customers, suppliers and shareholders are stakeholders, who may also report.

quiz.question: Which channels must the bank publicise for whistleblowing, at a minimum?
options: A direct telephone number, a website, postal service and an email address
An email address only, monitored by the HR department
A suggestion box in every branch and an annual staff survey
A meeting with the line manager, then a written letter to the CEO
quiz.explanation: Section III.a lists the minimum channels: a direct telephone number, website, postal service and email address.

quiz.question: An employee reports in good faith, but the investigation cannot establish the violation. What does the policy say?
options: The report is deleted and the employee is not told the outcome
No action will be taken against the whistleblower
The employee receives a formal warning for wasting resources
The employee must pay the cost of the investigation
quiz.explanation: Section III.a says that if a claim made in good faith is not established in the investigation, no action will be taken against the whistleblower.

quiz.question: To whom may Durrah Bank disclose information about a whistleblower?
options: To the media if the case becomes public
Only to competent authorities such as investigation and judicial bodies
To any manager who asks for a business reason
To the person reported, so he can respond
quiz.explanation: Section III.f says institutions shall not disclose information about a whistleblower except to competent authorities, such as investigation and judicial authorities.

quiz.question: A report arrives in English, poorly written and with few details. How must the bank treat it?
options: Return it until the reporter adds documents
Discard it unless the reporter gives a name
Seriously, whatever its language, adequacy of information, impact or importance
Log it but process it only if it is in Arabic
quiz.explanation: Section III.e requires the bank to treat every report with the necessary seriousness regardless of its nature, language, adequacy of information, impact or importance.

quiz.question: Which is the correct order of the first three processing stages in the policy?
options: Reception, decision, verification plan
Initial assessment, reception, decision
Verification plan, reception, record keeping
Reception, initial assessment, identification of a verification plan
quiz.explanation: Section III.g.5 lists reception, initial assessment, identification of the verification plan, documentation of the rationale, decision, follow-up and record keeping.

quiz.question: Who must approve a bank's whistleblowing policy?
options: The board of directors
The Chief Compliance Officer
The head of human resources
SAMA's consumer protection department
quiz.explanation: Section III.a requires a whistleblowing policy approved by the board of directors. The Key Principles of Governance also make the board responsible for a policy on reporting violations and protecting whistleblowers.

quiz.question: A whistleblower deliberately makes false claims to damage a colleague. What does the policy say?
options: Nothing, as all reporters are protected equally
The bank must still protect the reporter from any consequence
The bank must publish the reporter's name as a warning
The whistleblower bears responsibility for malicious allegations that defame or damage others
quiz.explanation: Section III.d makes the whistleblower responsible for malicious allegations that defame or damage the institution, its staff or stakeholders. Protection under III.f covers non-malicious reports.

quiz.question: What must each processing stage have under the policy's performance section?
options: An indicator measuring how far the stage meets the procedure's requirements
A target for the number of reports proven each year
A separate board approval for each case
A fee charged to the business unit reported
quiz.explanation: Section III.h requires a key performance indicator for each stage of the working procedures, measuring the extent to which each procedure's requirements are met.

sessions.title: Training, Certification and Readiness for a SAMA Review
sessions.summary: Bring it together: paragraph 72's annual compliance training and awareness programme for all staff, training new joiners before they start, periodic reminders for public-facing staff, SAMA's professional certificates in general terms, the risk-based compliance programme, documentation and the evidence a SAMA review will ask for.
objectives: Apply paragraph 72: the annual programme for all staff, training before new joiners start, and reminders for public-facing staff
Describe in general terms SAMA's professional certification requirement for front-line and credit staff
Explain the risk-based compliance programme, the compliance database and documentation duties
Assemble the governance, compliance, whistleblowing and training evidence a SAMA review expects

lines.text: SAMA's team arrives in three weeks. They want our compliance programme, training records and the last annual compliance report.
Al-Khobar hired twelve people last month. Four started at the counter before they did any compliance training. We were short-staffed.
My audit sample shows the same gap in two other branches. And the annual programme hasn't changed since the new circulars came out.
Speak-up awareness was last run eighteen months ago.
Then we have work to do. Final stage: the Review Room.

scenes.heading: Why train?
scenes.narration: Training all staff on the rules for their own jobs is how senior management builds a compliance culture and encourages staff to report violations to compliance.

scenes.heading: First line of defence
scenes.narration: The compliance unit helps senior management raise awareness, treating employees as the first line of defence, and answers their compliance questions.

scenes.heading: Written guidance
scenes.narration: Compliance helps produce written guidance: policies and procedures, compliance manuals, internal codes of conduct and practical guides.

scenes.heading: Annual programme
scenes.narration: There must be an annual training and awareness programme for all employees, planned to meet ongoing needs and quickly adjusted for new rules, findings or high staff turnover.

scenes.heading: Before day one
scenes.narration: New employees learn the compliance requirements of their banking work before they start their duties.

scenes.heading: Regular reminders
scenes.narration: Staff who deal directly with the public get periodic reminders on sales and marketing rules, AML/CTF, due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting and internal violations.

items.label: Before the first shift
items.detail: Compliance requirements of the job, taught before duties start.

items.label: First months
items.detail: Work towards the professional certificate SAMA requires for the role, within the period it sets.

items.label: Every year
items.detail: The bank's annual compliance training and awareness programme for all staff.

items.label: Through the year
items.detail: Reminders on sales, AML/CTF, due diligence, suspicious reports and internal violations.

items.label: When rules change
items.detail: Programme adjusted for new circulars, audit findings or high turnover.

cards.caption: Paragraph 72 of SAMA's compliance principles, with the professional certification circulars.

cards.question: A new relationship officer joins Durrah Bank on Sunday. When must she learn the compliance requirements of her work under paragraph 72?
options: Before she starts her duties
Within her first year
At the next annual training session
Only after her probation ends
cards.explanation: Paragraph 72 asks for training, especially for new employees, so they know the compliance requirements of their banking work before starting their duties.

cards.title: Which part of paragraph 72?
cards.prompt: Sort each training activity under the part of paragraph 72 it fulfils.

items.text: Yearly compliance e-learning and quiz for every employee
Updating the year's plan after a wave of resignations
Compliance module completed before a new teller serves customers
Induction briefing on the code of conduct before a new hire's first day
Monthly huddle reminding branch staff about sales and marketing rules
Short refresher for call-centre agents on reporting suspicious transactions
Adding a new SAMA circular to this year's programme
Reminder to tellers on due diligence and reporting internal violations

cards.title: Professional certificates, in general terms
Who trains, who signs?
cards.setting: Durrah Bank, Learning and Development. Tuesday afternoon.

lines.text: HR says onboarding has always been 'two weeks at the counter, then the classroom'. It's faster.
Faster, but it breaks paragraph 72. And nobody can show me who approved that design.
Senior management owns the training effort. Compliance helps design it and checks it works. Let's fix it properly.

cards.title: New joiners at the counter
cards.situation: Four new tellers at Al-Khobar served customers for two weeks before any compliance training, because of staff shortages. Two other branches show the same pattern. The SAMA review starts in three weeks.

choices.text: Train the affected tellers now, change onboarding so no one serves customers before compliance training, record the gap and the fix, and report it to senior management with the root cause.
choices.outcome: Best. Paragraph 72 requires new staff to learn the compliance requirements of their work before starting. Fixing the process, documenting it and reporting it shows a working compliance function, which matters more to a reviewer than a perfect record.

choices.text: Train the four tellers this week and leave the onboarding design as it is, since staffing is tight.
choices.outcome: Partly right: it closes today's gap but the same breach will repeat with the next hires.

choices.text: Backdate the training records to their start dates so the files look complete for SAMA.
choices.outcome: Poor. Falsifying records is a serious violation and destroys trust with the supervisor. It is also exactly the kind of conduct the whistleblowing policy asks staff to report.

choices.text: Explain to SAMA that the rule does not apply to tellers on temporary contracts.
choices.outcome: Poor. Paragraph 72 covers new employees generally, and SAMA's certification and conduct rules expressly reach staff contracted through third parties.

items.label: Risk-based compliance programme
items.detail: Planned activities overseen by the CCO, covering compliance, AML/CTF, fraud, corruption and violation reports.

items.label: Policies, risk assessment, testing
items.detail: Review policies, assess non-compliance risk, run compliance tests.

items.label: Awareness and training
items.detail: Annual programme, new joiner training, reminders, speak-up awareness.

items.label: Documentation
items.detail: Policies, plans, events and work papers documented; database of rules open to all staff.

items.label: Evidence for SAMA
items.detail: Reports, minutes, statistics and records that show it all works.
