cards.title: The annual compliance report cycle
cards.prompt: Put Durrah Bank's yearly steps in the order SAMA's compliance principles imply.
steps: Senior management, with compliance, assesses the main non-compliance risks for the year
The CCO runs the risk-based compliance programme, including tests and training
The CCO sends regular written reports to senior management on risks, breaches and fixes
Senior management prepares the annual compliance report for the board
The chairman sends the approved report to SAMA by the end of April

cards.question: Which statement about the compliance database in SAMA's principles is correct?
options: Only compliance staff may access it, to protect confidentiality
It must hold all compliance rules and standards, kept up to date and available to all employees
It replaces the need to explain new circulars to business units
It is optional for banks with fewer than ten branches
cards.explanation: Paragraph 84 requires a continuously updated database of all compliance regulations, rules and standards that all bank employees can access. Paragraph 65 still requires prompt communication to units.

cards.title: Your final boss checklist
Review Room take-aways
items: Paragraph 72 requires an annual compliance training and awareness programme for all staff, adjusted for new rules and turnover.
New employees learn the compliance requirements of their job before they start; public-facing staff get periodic reminders.
SAMA's professional certificates apply to front-line and credit staff, including third-party staff, within set periods; check the current circular.
The compliance programme is risk-based, documented and supported by a database of rules all staff can use.
A good SAMA review file shows policies, board approvals, reports, training and speak-up records that prove the system works.

cards.prompt: Pick one piece of evidence from this stage that your own unit would struggle to produce tomorrow. What would you change this month so it is ready?

quiz.question: Under paragraph 72, who should receive an annual compliance training and awareness programme?
options: Only new joiners in their first year
Only staff in customer-facing roles
Only compliance and internal audit staff
All employees of the bank
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 asks for an annual training and awareness programme for all employees, with extra emphasis on new joiners and public-facing staff.

quiz.question: Which event should prompt Durrah Bank to adjust its annual training programme during the year, according to paragraph 72?
options: The appointment of a new external auditor
A drop in branch footfall during holidays
High staff turnover or significant regulatory changes
A change in the bank's share price
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 says the plan must meet ongoing needs and be adjusted promptly for new issues, observations, significant changes or updates in regulations, or high employee turnover.

quiz.question: Which topic does paragraph 72 name for periodic reminders to staff who deal directly with the public?
options: Capital adequacy calculations
Board remuneration policy
Investment portfolio strategy
Suspicious transaction reporting
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 lists sales and marketing instructions, AML/CTF, due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions and internal violations as reminder topics for public-facing staff.

quiz.question: Who leads the training effort under paragraph 72, and what is compliance's role?
options: Senior management leads, and the compliance unit continuously and proactively assists it
The board designs the courses, and compliance delivers them
Compliance leads alone, and senior management is only informed
HR leads alone, and compliance has no role in training
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 describes training as a fundamental part of senior management's effort to build a compliance culture, with the compliance unit assisting proactively.

quiz.question: Which staff does SAMA's professional certification requirement expressly include, in general terms?
options: Front-line bank staff, including staff contracted through third parties
Only board members and senior executives
Only IT and cyber security staff
Only staff of the bank's overseas branches
quiz.explanation: SAMA's certification circulars cover front-line staff dealing with customers and staff granting credit to individuals, including people contracted through a third party.

quiz.question: Which certificate do SAMA's circulars require, in general terms, for staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals?
options: The board director certificate
The treasury dealer certificate
The credit adviser certificate
The internal audit certificate
quiz.explanation: The certification circulars require staff directly involved in granting credit to individuals, and branch managers, to hold the credit adviser certificate.

quiz.question: What must Durrah Bank's compliance programme be, according to paragraph 83?
options: Risk-based and overseen by the Chief Compliance Officer
Identical for every bank in the Kingdom
Approved by SAMA before it starts each year
Run by internal audit with compliance advice
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 83 says the compliance programme should be risk-based and overseen by the CCO, covering compliance monitoring, AML/CTF, fraud, corruption and violation reports.

quiz.question: What does paragraph 85 require the compliance unit to document?
options: Only matters escalated to SAMA
Policies, procedures, plans, events and work papers
Only the final annual compliance report
Only staff complaints about compliance
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 85 requires the compliance unit to document policies, procedures, plans, events and work papers to fulfil its duties.

quiz.question: A branch manager wants to run onboarding as 'two weeks at the counter, then training'. What is the best response?
options: Accept if the new staff shadow an experienced teller
Refuse: new staff must learn the compliance requirements of their job before starting their duties
Accept for temporary staff only
Accept if the training happens within the first month
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 requires new employees to be familiar with the compliance requirements of their work before they start their duties. Shadowing or later training does not meet that.

quiz.question: According to paragraph 72, what does training all staff aim to encourage besides a compliance culture?
options: Higher sales of new products
Reporting of violations to the compliance unit
Fewer meetings with SAMA
Less use of the compliance database
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 72 links training to instilling a compliance culture and encouraging staff to report violations to the compliance unit.

references.title: Principles of Compliance for Commercial Banks Operating in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
references.provision: Circular No. 42005223; Principles 1-10, paragraphs 17-99, esp. paragraph 72
references.note: Board, senior management and compliance unit duties; independence, rights and pay of the CCO and SAMA non-objection; annual report to SAMA by end of April; annual training programme for all staff, training before new joiners start and reminders for public-facing staff.

references.title: Key Principles of Governance in Financial Institutions Subject to Saudi Central Bank's Oversight and Supervision
references.provision: Version 2 (Circular No. 45068000, May 2024); Principles 1-5, incl. paragraphs 7, 19, 21, 36, 40, 43, 46 and 69-92
references.note: Board qualifications, size and independence, induction programme and memorandum of duties for every member, board duties towards control functions and whistleblowing policy, and the executive, audit, nomination and remuneration and risk committees.

references.title: Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions
references.note: SAMA written non-objection before board members and listed senior post holders act; minimum fit and proper criteria; at least annual reassessment; succession policy with training for Saudi candidates. The English page states it is not the latest version.

references.title: Whistle Blowing Policy for Financial Institutions
references.note: Board-approved policy, independent unit reporting to compliance, minimum channels, confidentiality and protection, awareness programmes, duties on receipt, processing stages, automated system and indicators.

references.title: Ensuring Continuous Fulfilment of the Professional Certification Requirement
references.note: Front-line bank staff need the retail banking fundamentals certificate and staff granting credit to individuals and branch managers the credit adviser certificate, including third-party staff, within a set period after employment.

references.title: Professional Certificates of Financial Institution Employees
references.note: Earlier circular making the updated professional certificates compulsory for front-line, sales, call-centre and customer care staff, including third-party staff.

references.title: Explanatory Statement by the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (Banque Saudi Fransi)
references.note: SAMA followed the board's steps to address deficiencies in applying sound governance and control policies.

references.title: Addendum statement from the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority regarding Saudi Fransi Bank
references.note: Inspection, independent examination team, end of an employee incentives programme, and fines for violations of sound governance and supervisory policies.

references.title: Statement by the Saudi Arabian Monetary Authority (National Commercial Bank salary deductions)
references.note: Fine on a bank that deducted more from salaries than permitted, with corrective action required.

references.title: SAMA imposes penalties on 30 financial institutions for violating the principles of responsible financing for individuals
references.note: Penalties on 30 named institutions, corrective action ordered, and a warning that the product could be stopped if violations continued.

references.title: SAMA announces the whistleblowing policy of financial institutions
references.note: Announcement of the policy setting minimum controls so staff and stakeholders can report violations without negative impact.

bank.question: Durrah Bank's board has delegated compliance oversight to its audit committee. Which yearly duty can that committee perform on the board's behalf under SAMA's compliance principles?
options: Appointing the Chief Compliance Officer without SAMA's non-objection
Approving its own exemption from the compliance policy
Evaluating the effectiveness of the bank's non-compliance risk management
Sending the annual compliance report to SAMA in place of the chairman
bank.explanation: Paragraph 33 allows the board or a committee it delegates to evaluate effectiveness at least once a year. The report goes to SAMA from the chairman, and the CCO's appointment needs SAMA's non-objection.

bank.question: A Saudi bank has a branch in another country whose law conflicts with one of SAMA's compliance principles. What do the principles say?
options: SAMA's principles always override host-country law
They apply to the foreign branch unless they conflict with that country's rules
They never apply outside the Kingdom
The branch may choose which rules to follow
bank.explanation: Paragraph 30 applies the principles to banks' branches and offices abroad unless they conflict with the host country's regulations; Principle 9 requires compliance with host-country law.

bank.question: Senior management at Durrah Bank sends the board a compliance report only every two years. Which requirement does this breach?
options: Monthly reports by the CCO to the general assembly
Quarterly reports to SAMA on every compliance test
A requirement to publish compliance reports on the bank's website
Written reports to the board or its delegated committee on non-compliance risk management at least once a year
bank.explanation: Paragraph 39 requires senior management, helped by compliance, to give the board or its delegated committee written reports on non-compliance risk management at least annually.

bank.question: Which statement best describes the compliance unit's role under paragraph 29 of SAMA's principles?
options: It performs internal audits of every branch on a sampling basis
It owns all controls in every business unit and corrects deficiencies itself
It approves every customer transaction above a set amount
It compiles, communicates and explains rules, confirms they are built into policies, monitors and assesses risk, and reports
bank.explanation: Paragraph 29 places managing non-compliance risk and controls on senior management and business units; the compliance unit communicates and explains rules, confirms inclusion in policies, monitors, assesses and reports.

bank.question: A bank's retail team keeps applying a practice that breaches SAMA instructions after compliance has flagged it twice. Based on SAMA's 2017 and 2020 statements on salary deductions and responsible financing, what is the most realistic regulatory outcome?
options: A private warning letter that is never published
Fines, public naming and an order to correct, with stronger measures if violations continue
Automatic loss of the bank's licence
No action, because consumer matters are handled only by courts
bank.explanation: SAMA fined the National Commercial Bank in 2017 and named 30 penalised institutions in 2020, ordering corrective action and warning that it could stop the product if violations continued.

bank.question: Which is NOT one of the sources of compliance rules and standards listed in SAMA's principles?
options: Internal sales targets set by business units
Instructions of other Saudi authorities with jurisdiction
Requirements issued by bodies such as the Basel Committee
Internal conduct rules applied to bank employees
bank.explanation: Paragraph 25 lists laws and SAMA instructions, other authorities' rules, host-country rules, banking practice, internal conduct rules, integrity standards and international standard setters. Sales targets are not a source of compliance rules.

bank.question: Who prepares the annual compliance report presented to the board under paragraph 79?
options: The external auditor
SAMA's supervision team
Senior management
The general assembly
bank.explanation: Paragraph 79 says senior management prepares the annual compliance report and presents it to the board, covering at least what SAMA requires from time to time.

bank.question: For a branch of a foreign bank in the Kingdom, who takes on the role the compliance principles give to the board of a local bank?
options: The home-country regulator
SAMA's bank supervision department
The branch's Chief Compliance Officer
The branch's chief officer
bank.explanation: The definitions say the primary officer of a foreign bank branch assumes the board's tasks and responsibilities wherever the principles refer to the board.

bank.question: Durrah Bank's compliance staff are asked to also approve loans in the retail credit unit during peak periods. Why does this conflict with SAMA's principles?
options: Compliance staff are not allowed to hold banking qualifications
It is fine if the loans are below a set amount
Loan approvals may only be made by board members
Compliance staff should hold only compliance responsibilities, to avoid conflicts of interest
bank.explanation: Paragraph 57 restricts the CCO and compliance unit staff to compliance responsibilities only; element three of independence rules out conflicting roles.

bank.question: A business head refuses to give compliance access to a customer file during an investigation, saying the data is sensitive. What do the principles say?
options: Compliance has the right to access any information, records and files it needs, without waiting for instructions
Only internal audit may access customer files
Compliance must obtain the business head's written consent first
Compliance must ask SAMA for permission to see the file
bank.explanation: Paragraph 59 gives the compliance unit the right to communicate with any employee and access any information, records and files it needs, without waiting for orders or instructions.

bank.question: The CCO wants to delegate compliance tasks in the bank's overseas office to a local employee. What remains true after delegation?
options: Accountability passes to internal audit
Accountability passes to the head of the overseas office
The CCO stays accountable for all compliance-related tasks
Accountability passes to the local employee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 56 allows the CCO to delegate some authority, but delegation does not exempt the CCO, who remains accountable for all compliance tasks.

bank.question: Durrah Bank has a New Products Committee. What do the compliance principles expect?
options: Representatives of the compliance unit should take part in the committee
Compliance must chair the committee and hold a veto
Compliance must be kept out to preserve independence
Only internal audit may sit on the committee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 73 says that where a bank has a New Products Committee, compliance unit representatives should participate in it, as part of identifying risks early.

bank.question: Which list matches the regulatory responsibilities paragraph 81 gives the compliance unit?
options: Compliance oversight, AML/CTF, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, self-supervision and handling violation reports
Credit approval, treasury dealing, AML/CTF and marketing
Internal audit, external audit, legal affairs and HR
Financial reporting, tax filing, AML/CTF and IT security
bank.explanation: Paragraph 81 lists compliance oversight, AML/CTF, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, self-supervision and handling violation reports.

bank.question: The compliance unit wants to measure non-compliance risk. Which approach matches paragraph 74?
options: Using quantitative and qualitative indicators, such as trends in complaints, fraud cases and penalties
Counting the circulars SAMA issues each quarter
Relying only on the number of training hours completed
Asking business units to rate their own compliance once a year
bank.explanation: Paragraph 74 asks the unit to measure non-compliance risk quantitatively and qualitatively, for example through indicators like rising complaints, fraud cases, reports and penalties.

bank.question: Which content must the CCO's regular written reports to senior management include under paragraph 77?
options: Only matters that SAMA has already raised
The personal performance ratings of business heads
Risk assessment for the period, changes in risk level, breaches found, proposed fixes and due dates, and actions taken
Only the number of staff trained during the period
bank.explanation: Paragraph 77 lists the assessment of non-compliance risk, changes shown by indicators, a summary of violations and deficiencies, proposed corrective actions with dates, and actions already taken.

bank.question: Who gives final approval of the Chief Compliance Officer's rewards?
options: The board of directors or one of its committees
SAMA's supervision department
The head of the retail division
The chief executive alone
bank.explanation: Paragraph 58 requires the final approval of rewards for the CCO and compliance unit staff to come from the board or a committee derived from it.

bank.question: Which document must set out the compliance unit's official status, so that all employees are told about it?
options: The compliance policy or an official document related to it
The employment contract of each compliance officer
The external auditor's management letter
The bank's annual financial statements
bank.explanation: Paragraph 47 requires the unit's official status to be set out in the compliance policy or a related official document, and all employees to be informed of it. Paragraph 48 lists its minimum contents.

bank.question: A bank's board has 10 members: two executive members, the CEO as chairman, and four independent members. Which feature breaches SAMA's Key Principles of Governance?
options: Having four independent members
Having two executive members
The CEO serving as chairman
Having ten members in total
bank.explanation: The principles require separation of the chairman and CEO roles, and the chairman and deputy must be non-executive. Two executives, ten members and four independents (more than one third) are within the limits.

bank.question: A non-executive director missed three board meetings this year without a valid reason. What do the Key Principles provide?
options: He loses his vote for the rest of the term
Another member is to be appointed to replace him
He receives a written warning from SAMA
Nothing, as attendance by technology is optional
bank.explanation: Paragraph 24 says that if a member fails to attend three meetings a year without a valid reason, another member shall be appointed to replace him.

bank.question: A director wants to join the board of another Saudi bank while staying on Durrah Bank's board. What do the Key Principles say?
options: It is allowed if both boards approve
It is allowed for up to five similar institutions
A member may not sit on the board of a similar financial institution operating in the Kingdom
It is allowed if he resigns from all committees
bank.explanation: Paragraph 13 bars a member from being on the board of a similar financial institution operating inside the Kingdom. The five-company limit in paragraph 14 relates to listed joint stock companies.

bank.question: Which committee should coordinate with HR on the replacement and succession policy?
options: The audit committee
The nomination and remuneration committee
The executive committee
The risk committee
bank.explanation: Paragraph 87 lists coordinating with HR on the replacement and succession policy among the nomination and remuneration committee's tasks.

bank.question: The audit committee reviews a SAMA inspection report. Which task under the 'compliance' heading of paragraph 82 does this fulfil?
options: Approving new products before SAMA sees them
Setting the pay of the Chief Compliance Officer
Reviewing the findings of supervisory reports and making sure the bank takes the necessary measures
Deciding which whistleblowing reports to investigate
bank.explanation: Under paragraph 82(d), the audit committee reviews supervisory authorities' report findings, ensures the bank acts on them, reports issues to the board and works to improve regulatory compliance.

bank.question: Durrah Bank enters into a transaction with a company owned by a board member's wife, worth 1.5% of the bank's total revenues in its latest audited statements. What do the Key Principles require?
options: Only a note in the next annual report
A commercial basis, and notifying the public and SAMA without delay
Approval from SAMA before the board can discuss it
Nothing, since the member is not personally a party
bank.explanation: Paragraph 43(f) requires related-party transactions to be on a commercial basis, and the public and SAMA to be notified without delay if the transaction equals or exceeds 1% of total revenues. A company owned by a member's relative is a related party.

bank.question: Under the senior appointment requirements, which of these Durrah Bank posts needs SAMA's written non-objection?
options: Director of Customer Care
Regional marketing coordinator
Call-centre team leader
Branch teller supervisor
bank.explanation: Appendix 1 lists senior posts in banks needing SAMA's non-objection, including the Director of Customer Care, alongside the CEO, CFO, CRO, CCO, head of internal audit and others.

bank.question: After SAMA has granted non-objection for a CFO, the bank learns he is under investigation abroad. What should it do?
options: Wait for the investigation to end before telling SAMA
Disclose the information to SAMA in writing promptly, as the requirements set a short deadline for such changes
Do nothing, since SAMA's non-objection already covers him
Mention it at the next annual fit and proper review
bank.explanation: The requirements oblige the bank to disclose to SAMA in writing any information relevant to fitness and propriety, even after non-objection, within a short set period, and to report material findings immediately.

bank.question: Why must Durrah Bank check the Arabic text of SAMA's Requirements for Appointments to Senior Positions before relying on detailed timelines?
options: The English version was withdrawn in 2019
The Arabic version applies only to Saudi candidates
SAMA publishes no English translation of the requirements
The English page in the SAMA Rulebook states that it is not the latest updated version
bank.explanation: The English page itself notes that the version displayed is not the last updated version and refers readers to the Arabic text.

bank.question: Which part of SAMA's 2017 statements about Banque Saudi Fransi best shows the board's role in fixing governance failures?
options: The board asked the external auditor to replace management
The board waited for the courts before making any change
The board left all corrective steps to SAMA's inspectors
The board took urgent decisions, including an independent examination team and stopping the incentives programme
bank.explanation: SAMA said it held several meetings with the board, which took urgent corrective decisions: an independent examination team, stopping the programme, reviewing the authority table, restructuring and new appointments.

bank.question: A customer emails Durrah Bank's speak-up address about a staff member who seems to be misusing bank property. Is the customer covered by SAMA's Whistle Blowing Policy?
options: No: only employees may use whistleblowing channels
No: customers must use the complaints process only
Yes: stakeholders such as customers may report violations under the policy
Only if the customer has an account above a set balance
bank.explanation: The policy's scope covers employees and stakeholders, defined as anyone with an interest in the institution, including shareholders, creditors, customers and suppliers.

bank.question: Which of the following is listed among the whistleblowing cases in SAMA's policy?
options: Disagreement with a manager's leave decision
Unlawful disclosure of confidential information
A late delivery from an office supplier
A customer's dislike of a product's design
bank.explanation: The cases include unlawful disclosure of confidential information, misuse of assets, abuse of power, conflicts of interest, breaches of law and policy, and others. The other options are not violations.

bank.question: Dana's unit receives a report and confirms the violation. Which action is the bank's duty under section III.e of the policy?
options: Publish the reporter's name to show the system works
Take corrective action for the proven violation and keep the report and documents for the required periods
Close the case without telling the reporter anything
Ask the person reported to approve the corrective action
bank.explanation: Section III.e requires the bank to take corrective action if a violation is proven, notify the reporter of receipt and if possible the decision, refer for investigation, keep records and prepare reports.

bank.question: An anonymous report arrives with no way to identify the sender. Later the sender claims retaliation protection. What does the policy say?
options: The bank must pay compensation to all anonymous reporters
Anonymous reports must be rejected on arrival
The bank must reveal who sent it to confirm the claim
A whistleblower whose identity was not revealed and could not be discovered may not claim the protection described
bank.explanation: Section III.f says a whistleblower whose identity was not revealed and could not be discovered by the institution cannot claim protection as described, since no one could have targeted them.

bank.question: Who must receive periodic reports on whistleblowing cases received and actions taken?
options: Every employee, through the intranet
The general assembly and the external auditor
The board of directors and the audit committee
SAMA's consumer protection department only
bank.explanation: Section III.a requires the institution to submit a periodic report on cases received and actions taken to its board of directors and audit committee.

bank.question: How does SAMA's compliance principles document connect to the whistleblowing policy?
options: The compliance principles replace the whistleblowing policy for banks
Handling violation reports is a compliance unit responsibility, and the red flags principle must protect whistleblowers and include incentives
Whistleblowing is handled only by HR and is outside compliance
Compliance may decide not to process reports about senior staff
bank.explanation: Paragraphs 27 and 81 list handling violation reports among compliance's duties, and paragraph 86 asks the warning-signs principle to protect whistleblowers and include incentives in line with SAMA's policy.

bank.question: Which statement about the timeline SAMA set when it issued the whistleblowing policy in 2019 is correct?
options: Institutions had three months to implement it and one month to give SAMA a compliance plan
It took effect only after each bank's general assembly approved it
Institutions had one year to implement it and no plan was required
It applied only to banks that had a whistleblowing case that year
bank.explanation: The policy's cover note asked institutions to implement it within three months of its date and to provide SAMA with a compliance plan within one month.

bank.question: A manager tells his team: 'Only report something if you are sure you can prove it.' Why is this message inconsistent with SAMA's policy?
options: The policy forbids managers from discussing whistleblowing
Proof is required, but only for reports about managers
Staff must report only to SAMA, not to the bank
The bank must encourage staff not to hold back because they are unsure whether a report can be supported with facts
bank.explanation: Section III.a asks institutions to encourage employees not to hesitate to report because they are uncertain whether it can be supported, while avoiding rumours and false allegations.

bank.question: Durrah Bank's annual training plan was set in January. In June, SAMA issues a major new circular and branch turnover doubles. What does paragraph 72 expect?
options: Cancel the annual programme and replace it with reminders
Wait for SAMA to send its own training materials
Keep the plan unchanged until next January
Adjust the programme promptly to cover the new circular and the turnover
bank.explanation: Paragraph 72 requires the annual plan to meet ongoing needs and be adjusted promptly for significant changes in regulation or high employee turnover.

bank.question: Which statement about SAMA's professional certificates is accurate in general terms?
options: They are optional for staff who completed the bank's own induction
They replace paragraph 72's annual compliance programme
They apply to front-line and credit staff, including third-party staff, within a set period after joining
They apply only to staff hired before 2019
bank.explanation: The certification circulars require certificates for front-line and credit staff, including third-party contractors, within a set period after employment. They add to, not replace, the bank's own compliance training.

bank.question: SAMA's reviewers ask how Durrah Bank makes sure staff can always find current rules. Which evidence best answers under the compliance principles?
options: A list of SAMA circulars filed in the CEO's office
The annual report's list of board committees
The compliance database of all rules and standards, kept up to date and open to all employees
The external auditor's letter on financial controls
bank.explanation: Paragraph 84 requires a continuously updated database of all compliance rules and standards that all employees can access at any time.

bank.question: Which combination best shows SAMA reviewers that Durrah Bank meets paragraph 72 for new joiners?
options: Onboarding design requiring compliance training before duties start, plus records of each joiner's training date and start date
The total training budget for the year
The number of courses in the learning catalogue
A signed statement from HR that onboarding is adequate
bank.explanation: Paragraph 72 requires training before new staff start; the strongest evidence links a process that enforces it to individual records comparing training and start dates.

bank.question: A reviewer asks who should drive the annual compliance training and awareness programme. Which answer reflects SAMA's documents?
options: The compliance unit alone decides and delivers it without management involvement
Internal audit designs and approves it
Each employee chooses whether to attend
Senior management leads it, compliance assists, and the board oversees training and awareness efforts
bank.explanation: Paragraph 72 frames training as senior management's effort assisted by compliance, and paragraph 32 asks the board to oversee efforts in training and awareness under the compliance policy.

bank.question: Durrah Bank relies heavily on staff supplied by an agency in its call centre. Which statement is correct?
options: Agency staff need certificates only if they work in branches
SAMA's certification and conduct rules expressly reach staff contracted through third parties
Only the agency, not the bank, answers for their training
Agency staff are outside all SAMA training rules
bank.explanation: SAMA's certification circulars include staff contracted through a third party, and the whistleblowing policy and conduct principles include third-party staff in their definitions of employees.

bank.question: Which item would a SAMA reviewer most likely use to test the board's role in governance training?
options: The canteen menu for training days
The induction programme and memorandum of duties given to each new board member
The number of compliance posters in branches
The marketing plan for the new card
bank.explanation: Paragraph 19 of the Key Principles requires an induction programme and a memorandum of duties for each member, which a reviewer can check directly.

bank.question: Which statement about paragraph 72's reminder duty is correct?
options: It targets staff who deal directly with the public and covers sales, AML/CTF, due diligence, suspicious reports and internal violations
It targets board members and covers only strategy
It targets IT staff and covers only cyber security
It applies only in a staff member's first month
bank.explanation: Paragraph 72 asks for periodic reminders to staff who deal directly with the public on sales and marketing instructions, AML/CTF, due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting and internal violations.
